question: Which of the following sets of species is isoelectronic with Argon (Z = 18)?
explanation: Argon has 18 electrons. Cl<sup>-</sup> (17+1), K<sup>+</sup> (19-1), and Ca<sup>2+</sup> (20-2) all possess 18 electrons.

question: Arrange the following isoelectronic ions in order of increasing ionic radius: O<sup>2-</sup>, F<sup>-</sup>, Na<sup>+</sup>, Mg<sup>2+</sup>.
explanation: As nuclear charge (Z) increases from Mg (12) to O (8), radius decreases. Thus Mg<sup>2+</sup> is smallest and O<sup>2-</sup> is largest.

question: How many electrons are present in the isoelectronic species N<sup>3-</sup>, O<sup>2-</sup>, and F<sup>-</sup>?
explanation: N (7+3=10), O (8+2=10), F (9+1=10); all contain 10 electrons.

question: Which species is isoelectronic with CO?
explanation: CO has 6 + 8 = 14 electrons. N<sub>2</sub> has 7 + 7 = 14 electrons.

question: In an isoelectronic series, effective nuclear charge (Z<sub>eff</sub>) ____.
explanation: Z<sub>eff</sub> increases with atomic number Z because nuclear charge increases while the shielding electron count remains constant.

question: Which of the following ions has the smallest radius?
explanation: All are isoelectronic with 10 electrons. Al<sup>3+</sup> has the highest nuclear charge (Z = 13), resulting in the smallest radius.

question: Which molecule is isoelectronic with NO<sup>+</sup>?
explanation: NO<sup>+</sup> has 7 + 8 - 1 = 14 electrons. N<sub>2</sub> has 14 electrons.

question: The ionic radii of isoelectronic ions follow which proportionality with atomic number Z?
explanation: Ionic radius is inversely proportional to nuclear charge Z in an isoelectronic series.

question: Which of the following contains 18 electrons?
explanation: Ca<sup>2+</sup> (20-2=18), K<sup>+</sup> (19-1=18), and Cl<sup>-</sup> (17+1=18) all have 18 electrons.

question: Which species is isoelectronic with the hydronium ion (H<sub>3</sub>O<sup>+</sup>)?
explanation: H<sub>3</sub>O<sup>+</sup> has 3(1) + 8 - 1 = 10 electrons. NH<sub>3</sub> has 7 + 3(1) = 10 electrons.

question: Which ion has the largest radius in the series S<sup>2-</sup>, Cl<sup>-</sup>, K<sup>+</sup>, Ca<sup>2+</sup>?
explanation: S<sup>2-</sup> has the lowest nuclear charge (Z = 16) among the 18-electron isoelectronic series, giving it the largest radius.

question: Between Na<sup>+</sup> and F<sup>-</sup>, which has a smaller radius?
explanation: Na<sup>+</sup> has Z = 11 while F<sup>-</sup> has Z = 9. Higher nuclear charge in Na<sup>+</sup> pulls the 10 electrons closer.

question: Which of the following pairs represents isoelectronic species with 36 electrons?
explanation: Kr has atomic number 36. Br<sup>-</sup> has 35 + 1 = 36 electrons.

question: What is the total number of electrons in the sulfate ion (SO<sub>4</sub><sup>2-</sup>)?
Which property generally decreases across an isoelectronic series from anion to cation?
explanation: Ionic radius decreases progressively from anion to cation in an isoelectronic series.

question: Which of the following is isoelectronic with cyanide ion (CN<sup>-</sup>)?
explanation: CN<sup>-</sup> has 6 + 7 + 1 = 14 electrons. Both N<sub>2</sub> (14) and CO (14) are isoelectronic with it.

question: Which of the following sets contains only isoelectronic species?
explanation: N<sup>3-</sup> (10), O<sup>2-</sup> (10), and Ne (10) all have exactly 10 electrons.
